papers.title: Machine Learning-Guided Discovery of Natural BACE1 Inhibitors with Enzymatic and Cellular Validation.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease characterized by excessive accumulation of β-amyloid (Aβ) peptides in the brain. Beta-secretase 1 (BACE1), the rate-limiting enzyme in the amyloidogenic processing pathway of amyloid precursor protein (APP), has been widely recognized as an important therapeutic target for reducing Aβ production. In the present study, nine machine learning-based predictive models for BACE1 inhibitors were constructed using Naïve Bayes (NB) and Recursive Partitioning (RP) algorithms. Subsequently, internal and external validations were conducte
papers.summary: This study built nine machine learning models (using Naïve Bayes and Recursive Partitioning) to predict BACE1 inhibitors, a key enzyme target for reducing β-amyloid production in Alzheimer's disease. The models were validated internally and externally, and predicted natural compounds were confirmed through enzymatic and cellular assays. This demonstrates a practical ML-guided pipeline for discovering natural-product BACE1 inhibitors.

papers.title: MacroTox: A Macroscopic Graph Topology-Based Multimodal Learning Framework for Robust Molecular Toxicity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Despite breakthroughs in predicting acute organ toxicities, advanced computational models continue to struggle with complex, insidious end points like drug-induced bone toxicity. A fundamental limitation of most supervised pipelines is their failure to explicitly model intermolecular similarities during task-specific training. Neglecting this macroscopic topology of the chemical space leads to fragmented latent representations, poor generalization, and high false negative rates. To address this, we propose MacroTox, a macroscopic topology-driven multimodal deep learning framework. Beyond intra
papers.summary: MacroTox is a multimodal deep learning framework that explicitly models intermolecular similarities (macroscopic topology of chemical space) during training to improve molecular toxicity prediction, particularly for complex endpoints like drug-induced bone toxicity. By incorporating this macroscopic graph topology, it aims to produce more coherent latent representations, better generalization, and lower false negative rates than standard supervised pipelines.

papers.title: Genome-wide-scale prediction of compound-protein interactions using foundation and language models based on three-dimensional structures of compounds and proteins.
papers.abstract: The identification of compound-protein interactions (CPIs) is crucial in the early stages of drug discovery. However, machine-learning (ML)-based methods based on one- and two-dimensional representations cannot capture important geometric information on the binding sites of CPIs, which limits their predictive accuracy.
papers.summary: This paper presents a machine-learning approach for predicting compound-protein interactions (CPIs) at genome-wide scale by leveraging foundation and language models that incorporate the three-dimensional structures of both compounds and proteins. The method addresses a key limitation of prior 1D/2D representation-based models, which fail to capture geometric binding-site information, thereby improving predictive accuracy for early-stage drug discovery.

papers.title: Lipid tail length dictates membrane disruption by carmofur analogs and reveals noncanonical modes of action.
papers.abstract: Carmofur, a lipidated urethane derivative and prodrug of 5-fluorouracil, has an established clinical application as an antineoplastic agent for the treatment of colorectal cancer, primarily through inhibition of acid ceramidase and subsequent intracellular drug release. Beyond this oncological application, recent drug repurposing efforts have identified covalent inhibition of the SARS-CoV-2 main protease as an additional antiviral mechanism. The pronounced amphiphilic character of carmofur, arising from a polar fluoropyrimidine headgroup appended to a hydrophobic aliphatic tail, raises the pos
papers.summary: This study examines how the length of the lipid tail in carmofur analogs affects their ability to disrupt membranes, revealing that tail length is a key determinant of membrane activity. The findings suggest that carmofur and its analogs may act through noncanonical mechanisms beyond their known targets, such as acid ceramidase and the SARS-CoV-2 main protease.

papers.title: Quinazoline-tethered thiazolo[3,2-a]pyrimidines and their cyclic chalcone derivatives as HIV-1 reverse transcriptase inhibitors: green synthesis, molecular docking, and in silico studies.
papers.abstract: Nitrogen-fused heterocycles have attracted considerable research interest in pharmaceutical, medicinal, organometallic, and materials chemistry. In this work, two new series of quinazoline-linked thiazolo[3,2-a]pyrimidines and their cyclic chalcone derivatives were synthesized using choline hydroxide as an environmentally friendly catalyst. The synthesized compounds were evaluated for their inhibitory activity against HIV-1 reverse transcriptase (RT). Compound 11e showed the highest inhibitory activity, with an IC50 value of 0.599 µg mL-1 (1.305 µM). Molecular docking was performed to examine
papers.summary: The authors synthesized two new series of quinazoline-linked thiazolo[3,2-a]pyrimidines and cyclic chalcone derivatives using a green choline hydroxide catalyst, then tested them as HIV-1 reverse transcriptase inhibitors. Compound 11e was the most potent with an IC50 of 0.599 µg/mL (1.305 µM), and molecular docking was used to explore its binding interactions with the enzyme.

papers.title: Design, synthesis, and preliminary anticancer evaluation of diphenylpropan-1-one derivatives: in vitro, in vivo and in silico studies.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer is a leading cause of cancer-associated mortality and morbidity worldwide, and there is a continued need for structurally diverse anticancer agents with improved properties. The present study reports a series of diphenylpropan-1-one (DPP) derivatives (4a-4i), rationally designed around a chalcone framework and synthesized via a three-step reaction sequence. The physicochemical and spectral characterization of the synthesized derivatives was performed using spectral techniques. Their anticancer potential was evaluated through a preliminary in vitro cytotoxicity screening against t
papers.summary: This study reports the design and synthesis of nine diphenylpropan-1-one derivatives based on a chalcone scaffold, followed by preliminary anticancer testing. The compounds were evaluated for cytotoxicity against breast cancer cells in vitro, with additional in vivo and computational (in silico) analyses. The work aims to identify new structurally diverse anticancer candidates, though the abstract is truncated and detailed results are not fully described.

papers.title: Rational High-Throughput Screening of Cocrystals: An Explainable Deep Learning Framework Based on Morgan Fingerprints and Cross-Attention.
papers.abstract: Aiming to address the problems of high blindness in traditional screening methods, insufficient granularity of feature representation, and poor interpretability of existing machine learning prediction models in the field of cocrystal research and development, we propose a cocrystal prediction method based on Morgan fingerprints and the cross-attention mechanism. First, a high-quality cocrystal data set is constructed, and Morgan fingerprints are employed to characterize molecular structures. Subsequently, a fingerprint-driven cross-attention model is developed to capture the feature interactio
papers.summary: The authors developed an explainable deep learning framework that predicts cocrystal formation by combining Morgan fingerprints with a cross-attention mechanism. By building a high-quality cocrystal dataset and capturing feature interactions between molecular pairs, the model aims to reduce the trial-and-error nature of traditional cocrystal screening while improving interpretability.

papers.title: Discovery of Selective Small-Molecule Ligands of SV2C by AI-Enhanced Virtual Screening and Experimental Validation.
papers.abstract: Synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2C (SV2C) is enriched in dopaminergic neurons and implicated in Parkinson's disease, but no selective small-molecule probes exist for it. Lacking a full-length SV2C structure, we built a homology model from SV2A cryo-EM templates and used molecular dynamics to characterize its conformational landscape. An AI-enhanced virtual screening pipeline, validated on a curated SV2A benchmark, was applied to 5.96 million commercial compounds, prioritizing 94 candidates for experimental testing. Of 71 compounds tested in an orthogonal biophysical assay cascade, 22 were active
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Researchers built a homology model of the SV2C protein, which is linked to Parkinson's disease but lacked selective chemical probes, and used AI-enhanced virtual screening of 5.96 million compounds to identify potential binders. Experimental testing of 94 prioritized candidates yielded 22 active compounds, providing a starting point for developing selective SV2C ligands.

papers.title: Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Reveals Immune Dysregulation and Candidate Drug Targets in Endometriosis.
papers.abstract: Endometriosis is a chronic inflammatory disorder affecting 5-10% of women of reproductive age and is associated with chronic pain and infertility. While research has mainly focused on local lesions, systemic immune dysfunction is increasingly implicated in disease pathogenesis. This study employs single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from women with endometriosis and unaffected controls, combined with integrative analysis of publicly available datasets of menstrual blood and endometrial tissues, to uncover immune dysregulation and therapeutic targ
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing of peripheral blood mononuclear cells from women with endometriosis and controls, combined with public datasets of menstrual blood and endometrial tissue, to characterize systemic immune dysregulation. The analysis identifies altered immune cell populations and candidate drug targets, suggesting that endometriosis involves broader immune dysfunction beyond local lesions.

papers.title: Benzamides of 2-(aminophenyl)benzimidazoles and 2-(aminophenyl)indoles as Anticancer Scaffolds: Synthesis, In Silico and In Vitro Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Indoles and benzimidazoles are important nitrogen-containing heterocyclic scaffolds and are a cornerstone of synthetic drugs. In this study, benzamides of 2-aminophenylindoles and 2-aminophenylbenzimidazoles were synthesized and evaluated for their potential. Further, they were also subjected to computational studies for their ADMET profiling and binding with target proteins. Methods: The synthesized compounds were characterized by ATR-FTIR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR and electrospray ionization mass spectroscopy (ESI-MS). They were screened for their in vitro antibacterial activit
papers.summary: This study synthesized a series of benzamide derivatives of 2-(aminophenyl)benzimidazoles and 2-(aminophenyl)indoles and evaluated them for anticancer potential. The compounds were characterized spectroscopically, tested in vitro for antibacterial activity, and subjected to in silico ADMET profiling and molecular docking against target proteins. The work identifies these scaffolds as promising starting points for further anticancer drug development.

papers.title: Cracking ERα Y537S Resistance: Explainable Machine Learning-Guided Discovery and Molecular Dynamics Validation of Stable Candidate Ligands.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Endocrine resistance due to activating mutations in the estrogen receptor alpha (ERα), especially Y537S, is still a big challenge in the treatment of hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, and there is a need to develop new small-molecule inhibitors that can overcome ligand-independent receptor activation. We used an integrated machine learning and molecular dynamics (MD)-based virtual screening (VS) approach to identify potential computationally prioritized hits of ERα Y537S in this study. Methods: The dataset (~3353 compounds) was characterized using molecular finger
papers.summary: This study combines explainable machine learning with molecular dynamics simulations to discover small-molecule inhibitors that can overcome the Y537S mutation in estrogen receptor alpha, a key driver of endocrine resistance in breast cancer. The authors screened ~3,353 compounds and prioritized candidate ligands that remain stably bound to the mutant receptor, offering a computational pipeline for tackling drug-resistant ERα variants.

papers.title: Virtual Screening and Molecular Dynamics Simulations Identifying Natural Product-Derived Cathepsin K Inhibitors as Potential Therapeutics for Osteoporosis.
papers.abstract: Osteoporosis is a prevalent skeletal disorder characterized by excessive bone resorption and an increased risk of fragility fracture. Cathepsin K (CatK), a lysosomal cysteine protease predominantly expressed in osteoclasts, is an established target for anti-resorptive drug development. Here, an integrated computational workflow comprising virtual screening, molecular docking, 300 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, molecular mechanics/Poisson-Boltzmann surface area (MM/PBSA) calculations, and drug-likeness/ADMET prediction was used to prioritize natural product-derived CatK ligands from th
papers.summary: This study used an integrated computational pipeline—virtual screening, molecular docking, 300 ns molecular dynamics simulations, MM/PBSA binding free energy calculations, and ADMET prediction—to identify natural product-derived compounds that inhibit cathepsin K, a protease target for osteoporosis therapy. The workflow prioritized candidate ligands with favorable binding stability and drug-like properties, nominating them for further experimental validation.

papers.title: Donor-Type-Dependent Heterogeneity of Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury in Lung Transplantation: A Multi-Cohort Transcriptomic Interaction Analysis of DCD Versus DBD Lungs.
papers.abstract: Donation after circulatory death (DCD) and donation after brain death (DBD) donor lungs are widely used in lung transplantation yet managed as equivalent with respect to ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI), despite fundamentally different ischemic backgrounds: warm ischemia in DCD versus neurogenic-inflammatory priming in DBD donors.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-cohort transcriptomic interaction analysis to show that ischemia-reperfusion injury in lung transplantation differs mechanistically between donation after circulatory death (DCD) and donation after brain death (DBD) donors. The findings suggest DCD and DBD lungs should not be managed as equivalent, since their distinct ischemic backgrounds (warm ischemia vs. neurogenic-inflammatory priming) drive donor-type-specific injury responses.

papers.title: KAN-GIN: Adaptive Nonlinear Molecular Representation Learning for Drug-Target Affinity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Accurate drug-target affinity (DTA) prediction supports virtual screening, lead optimization, and drug repurposing. This study investigates whether replacing the conventional post-aggregation multilayer perceptron within a Graph Isomorphism Network drug encoder with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) transformation improves DTA prediction. Methods: The resulting KAN-GIN framework combines molecular-graph representations with a convolutional protein-sequence encoder. It was evaluated on the DAVIS, KIBA, and METZ benchmarks against a matched GIN baseline and representative
papers.summary: This study introduces KAN-GIN, a drug-target affinity prediction framework that replaces the standard multilayer perceptron in a Graph Isomorphism Network drug encoder with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network transformation, paired with a convolutional protein-sequence encoder. Evaluated on DAVIS, KIBA, and METZ benchmarks against a matched GIN baseline and other representative methods, it tests whether adaptive nonlinear transformations improve affinity prediction.

papers.title: Multi-Endpoint Prediction of Bioactivity and ADMET Properties Coupled with Multi-Objective Optimization in Molecular Descriptor Space for Candidate ERα Antagonists.
papers.abstract: Objectives: Candidate estrogen receptor alpha (ERα) antagonists should combine strong inhibitory activity with favorable absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET)-related properties. This study developed an integrated framework for multi-endpoint prediction, multi-objective optimization in molecular descriptor space, and prioritization of feasible solutions. Methods: A dataset of 1974 compounds with 729 molecular descriptors, pIC50 values, and five binary ADMET-related endpoints was analyzed. Key descriptors were identified through two-stage cross-method and cross-e
papers.summary: This study builds an integrated computational framework that simultaneously predicts ERα antagonist bioactivity (pIC50) and five ADMET-related endpoints from molecular descriptors, then uses multi-objective optimization to prioritize candidate compounds balancing potency and drug-likeness. Using a dataset of 1974 compounds and 729 descriptors, the authors identify key features and generate feasible candidate solutions for ERα antagonist development. The work demonstrates how multi-endpoint modeling coupled with Pareto-style optimization can streamline early-stage drug discovery.

papers.title: Molecular Docking of Natural Products: Critical Appraisal of Current Methodology and Practical Guidelines.
papers.abstract: Molecular docking is among the most widely used techniques in structure-based drug discovery and has become integral to natural-product research. Despite substantial advances in computational algorithms and artificial intelligence, the methodological quality of published docking studies on natural compounds remains highly variable, and generally accepted methodological guidelines have yet to be established. This review critically evaluates current approaches to molecular docking of natural compounds, examines the specific features of different natural-product classes and protein targets, and o
papers.summary: This review critically evaluates the current state of molecular docking studies on natural products, highlighting that methodological quality remains highly variable despite advances in algorithms and AI. It examines how different natural-product classes and protein targets require tailored docking approaches and calls for standardized guidelines to improve reproducibility and reliability.

papers.title: Retrieval-Guided Transfer Learning for Low-Resource Ebola Drug-Target Affinity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Drug-target affinity (DTA) prediction plays an important role in computational drug discovery; however, its application to emerging infectious diseases such as Ebola remains challenging because of the limited availability of experimentally measured affinity data. To address this low-resource setting, we propose a retrieval-guided transfer-learning framework that leverages BindingDB interactions to improve Ebola DTA prediction. The framework uses a two-stage strategy. In Stage I, source interactions are selected using random sampling, compound-similarity retrieval, protein-similarity retrieval,
papers.summary: This paper introduces a retrieval-guided transfer-learning framework for predicting drug-target binding affinity (DTA) in Ebola, where experimental affinity data are scarce. It leverages the large BindingDB interaction dataset and selects source interactions via random sampling or compound/protein-similarity retrieval to pretrain models before fine-tuning on Ebola data. The approach aims to improve DTA prediction in low-resource infectious disease settings.

papers.title: Confidence-Gated Triage: Coupling Drug-Target Affinity and ADME-T Predictions to Prioritise Compounds for Docking.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Molecular docking and molecular dynamics are accurate but computationally expensive, so the compounds entering them must be chosen well. The present study proposes CADT, a confidence-gated affinity-ADME-T docking-triage cascade that decides which compounds are worth docking. Methods: The gate combines an ensemble estimate of drug-target affinity with its epistemic uncertainty and an applicability-domain check. Predicted absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADME-T) developability is added as a soft flag. All components were trained on openly lice
papers.summary: The authors present CADT, a triage cascade that uses an ensemble drug-target affinity model with epistemic uncertainty and applicability-domain checks, plus ADME-T developability predictions, to decide which compounds are worth the cost of docking. The confidence gate aims to filter out unreliable or unpromising compounds before expensive docking and molecular dynamics simulations.

papers.title: Integrated Machine Learning and Molecular Simulation-Guided Discovery of Novel Small-Molecule PD-L1 Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The programmed death-1/programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-1/PD-L1) immune checkpoint is a key therapeutic target in cancer immunotherapy, but small-molecule inhibition remains challenging due to its shallow and dynamic interaction interface. This study aimed to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-guided workflow to identify novel small-molecule inhibitors targeting the PD-L1 dimer interface. Methods: A combined computational and experimental approach was established. A support vector regression-genetic algorithm (SVR-GA) model was trained on a dataset of 1385 known PD-L1
papers.summary: This study developed an AI-guided workflow combining a support vector regression-genetic algorithm model with molecular simulations to discover novel small-molecule inhibitors targeting the PD-L1 dimer interface for cancer immunotherapy. The approach addresses the challenge of the shallow, dynamic PD-1/PD-L1 interaction interface that has made small-molecule inhibition difficult.

papers.title: Big Data and Artificial Intelligence in Cancer Drug Discovery: Promise, Challenges, and Emerging Opportunities.
papers.abstract: Oncologic drug development is lengthy (~14 years) and expensive (~1.2 billion USD) with low clinical trial success rates (4.1%). Big data and artificial intelligence (AI) are widely proposed as tools to address these challenges. In this review, we examine the current performance and future potential of big data and AI applied to preclinical discovery and development, clinical trials, and the regulatory approval process. We first examine the data foundation required for effective AI, including data harmonization, data commons, and analytical tools. We then assess preclinical applications spanni
papers.summary: This review examines how big data and AI are being applied across the cancer drug development pipeline, from preclinical discovery through clinical trials and regulatory approval. It highlights the data infrastructure requirements (harmonization, data commons, analytical tools) needed for effective AI, while assessing both the promise and current limitations of these approaches in addressing the lengthy, expensive, and low-success nature of oncology drug development.

papers.title: Development of an Interpretable QSAR Model for Predicting Coagulation Factor XIIa Inhibitors Using Ensemble Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: Background/Objective: Activated coagulation factor XII (FXIIa) is a component of the contact activation pathway and a pharmacologically relevant target in contact-system-associated processes. In this study, scaffold-aware and interpretable machine-learning QSAR models were developed for human FXIIa activity. Methods: Bioactivity records for the human single protein target CHEMBL2821 were retrieved from ChEMBL release 37. Modeling was restricted to exact IC50 measurements from assays explicitly referring to FXIIa, Factor XIIa, or activated Factor XII. Median-consolidated pIC50 values and two-di
papers.summary: This study developed interpretable QSAR models to predict inhibition of coagulation factor XIIa (FXIIa), a drug target in the contact activation pathway, using ensemble machine learning on ChEMBL bioactivity data. The models use scaffold-aware validation and provide interpretable features, supporting structure-based design of FXIIa inhibitors.

papers.title: A Transferable Genomic Language Model Framework for Fungal Gene Essentiality Prediction.
papers.abstract: Predicting biological function from genomic sequence remains a major challenge in computational and systems biology. Here, we tested whether the genomic language model Evo2, which encodes context-dependent DNA sequence patterns into embeddings, enables prediction of essential genes in fungi, a phenotype central to fungal biology and antifungal target discovery. We found that model performance was constrained not by the type or complexity of the downstream classifier, but by the biological information contained in Evo2 DNA embeddings. Specifically, the information recoverable from these embeddi
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study tests whether the genomic language model Evo2 can predict essential genes in fungi using DNA sequence embeddings. The authors find that prediction performance is limited primarily by the biological information encoded in Evo2's embeddings rather than by the choice of downstream classifier. This suggests current genomic language models may not capture sufficient functional signal for reliable essentiality prediction.

papers.title: Multiscale cross modal fusion and cascaded signal propagation for drug target interaction prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-target interaction (DTI) facilitates the translation of lead compounds into clinical therapeutics. Despite progress in deep learning, two challenges remain: the representation gap between heterogeneous drug and protein modalities and insufficient use of complementary knowledge from pretrained encoders. To address these issues, we propose SF-DTI, a unified framework that integrates multi-encoder protein fusion, structure-semantic drug alignment, and progressive cross-modal refinement for DTI prediction. Specifically, SF-DTI captures global protein semantics from mult
papers.summary: The paper introduces SF-DTI, a deep learning framework for predicting drug-target interactions that combines multiple protein encoders, aligns drug structure with semantic representations, and progressively refines cross-modal features. It aims to bridge the representation gap between heterogeneous drug and protein data and better exploit pretrained encoders, potentially improving DTI prediction accuracy.

papers.title: Cryptotanshinone and 15,16-dihydrotanshinone I from Salvia miltiorrhiza: integrated in vitro and computational evaluation of their antidiabetic potential.
papers.abstract: Salvia miltiorrhiza Bunge (Lamiaceae) is a traditional medicinal plant rich in bioactive tanshinones with diverse pharmacological properties. However, comparative information regarding experimentally measured activity and computational interaction profiles of individual tanshinones remains limited. This study aimed to compare cryptotanshinone (1) and 15,16-dihydrotanshinone I (2), isolated from S. miltiorrhiza, using an integrated in vitro and computational approach. The compounds were obtained through activity-informed phytochemical fractionation and evaluated for inhibition of α-glucosidase
papers.summary: This study isolated two tanshinone compounds (cryptotanshinone and 15,16-dihydrotanshinone I) from the traditional medicinal plant Salvia miltiorrhiza and evaluated their antidiabetic potential by testing their ability to inhibit the enzyme α-glucosidase in vitro, combined with computational docking analyses. The work provides a comparative profile of the two compounds' enzyme inhibition activity and predicted binding interactions, helping clarify which tanshinone may be more promising as an antidiabetic lead.

papers.title: Discovery and Biological Characterization of 1-[4-(2-Difluoromethoxyphenyl)-5-methylthiazol-2-yl]-3-(naphthalen-1-yl)urea (DFMNTU): A Novel Thiazolyl-Urea Chemotype Targeting Yellow Fever Virus and Host Casein Kinase 2 (CK2).
papers.abstract: Yellow fever virus (YFV) is a re- emerging mosquito- borne flavivirus that causes severe hemorrhagic fever with high case- fatality rates. Due to vaccine contraindications, incomplete immunization coverage, and the absence of approved specific antivirals, host- directed drug discovery targeting cellular machinery exploited by YFV is a critical therapeutic priority. Here, 1-[4-(2- difluoromethoxyphenyl)- 5- methylthiazol- 2- yl]- 3-(naphthalen- 1- yl)urea (DFMNTU) was synthesized, characterized by NMR, MS, and HPLC, and evaluated for antiviral efficacy against YFV strain 17 D in Vero cells. DFM
papers.journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
papers.summary: This paper reports the synthesis and characterization of DFMNTU, a novel thiazolyl-urea compound that targets yellow fever virus by inhibiting the host protein casein kinase 2 (CK2). The compound showed antiviral activity against YFV strain 17D in cell culture, suggesting host-directed antiviral strategies may be viable for flaviviruses.

papers.title: pLM-HP: Peptide hormone prediction using pre-trained protein language model representations.
papers.abstract: Peptide hormones play key roles in metabolic regulation, growth and development, and the maintenance of homeostasis and are important targets for drug discovery and design. However, traditional experimental methods for screening and identifying peptide hormones are costly and inefficient. Although existing machine learning methods have made some progress, they pay limited attention to class imbalance, and there is still room to improve prediction performance.
papers.summary: The paper introduces pLM-HP, a machine learning method that uses representations from a pre-trained protein language model to predict peptide hormones. It specifically addresses class imbalance, a common problem in this prediction task, and aims to improve on existing methods. The work is positioned as a computational tool for identifying peptide hormones relevant to drug discovery.

papers.title: Novel Flavonoid Senotherapeutics Identified by Phenotypic Drug Discovery Reduce Senescence and Improve Multiple Markers of Healthspan.
papers.abstract: Senescent cells are a key driver of aging and contribute to many age-related diseases. Senolytics, agents that selectively eliminate senescent cells, offer a promising therapeutic strategy to treat age-related diseases but face significant barriers to clinical translation. Fisetin, a natural flavonoid senolytic, has progressed to clinical trials but is limited by suboptimal efficacy and poor bioavailability. To address these challenges, we developed two novel fisetin-derived flavonoid senolytics, SR29384 and SR31133, using an integrative phenotypic drug discovery approach. These compounds exhi
papers.summary: Researchers developed two novel fisetin-derived flavonoid senolytics, SR29384 and SR31133, using an integrative phenotypic drug discovery approach. These compounds reduce senescence and improve multiple markers of healthspan, potentially overcoming the poor efficacy and bioavailability that limit fisetin's clinical translation.

papers.title: Discovery of PIM-1 kinase inhibitors from marine natural products through machine learning and structure-based screening.
papers.abstract: PIM-1 kinase, a serine/threonine kinase implicated in several cancers, has emerged as a promising yet underexplored target for anticancer therapy. This study aimed to identify the potential of PIM-1 inhibitors from marine natural products by integrating machine learning (ML)-based quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling with structure-based virtual screening.
papers.summary: This study combines machine learning-based QSAR modeling with structure-based virtual screening to identify PIM-1 kinase inhibitors from marine natural products. PIM-1 is a promising anticancer target, and the integrated computational approach was used to prioritize candidate compounds from marine sources for further development.

papers.title: A multiparametric in vitro strategy for small molecule drug-induced liver injury risk mitigation in early drug development.
papers.abstract: Drug-induced liver injury (DILI) remains a major cause of preclinical and clinical attrition, reflecting persistent gaps in the predictive translation of preclinical safety data to human outcomes. To address these gaps, we established a refined multiparametric framework for early DILI risk prediction using a balanced reference set of 170 drugs with established clinical outcomes. Thirty physicochemical, mechanistic endpoints, and exposure-related features were systematically evaluated to identify high-specificity predictors of intrinsic DILI risk. Cytotoxicity in primary human hepatocytes and h
papers.journal: Toxicological sciences : an official journal of the Society of Toxicology
papers.summary: This study establishes a multiparametric in vitro framework for predicting drug-induced liver injury (DILI) risk using a balanced reference set of 170 drugs with known clinical outcomes. By systematically evaluating 30 physicochemical, mechanistic, and exposure-related features, the authors identify high-specificity predictors, including cytotoxicity in primary human hepatocytes, to improve early-stage DILI risk mitigation in drug development.

papers.title: Beyond affinity: AI-supported developability assessment and multi-objective optimization in antibody development.
papers.abstract: Therapeutic antibodies are a major class of medicines, but high target affinity alone does not ensure manufacturability, stability, safety, or clinical success. Developability has therefore become a central constraint in antibody engineering and has pushed the field beyond affinity-first screening toward multi-objective decision-making. Machine-learning-based models increasingly integrate antibody sequence, structure, interaction, and assay data to estimate properties such as affinity, specificity, aggregation, viscosity, solubility, stability, immunogenicity, and pharmacokinetics before exper
papers.summary: This review argues that therapeutic antibody development must move beyond simple affinity optimization to consider manufacturability, stability, safety, and other developability properties. It surveys how machine-learning models integrate sequence, structure, interaction, and assay data to predict these properties and support multi-objective decision-making before experimental work.

papers.title: GCF-anchored and target-oriented mining of metagenomic BGC space for bioactive product discovery.
papers.abstract: Microbial natural products are vital for drug discovery, yet pervasive genomic fragmentation and data volume hinder the translation of metagenomic biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) into therapeutic leads. We present metasynBGC, a target-oriented framework that employs a "function-first" logic using experimentally validated gene cluster families (GCFs) as evolutionary templates and functional beacons. This dual-path strategy enables (i) template-guided reconstruction of fragmented BGCs via conserved biosynthetic synteny, and (ii) high-resolution prioritization of complete BGCs based on therapeu
papers.summary: The authors present metasynBGC, a target-oriented framework for mining metagenomic biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) that uses experimentally validated gene cluster families (GCFs) as evolutionary templates and functional beacons. The dual-path strategy enables template-guided reconstruction of fragmented BGCs and high-resolution prioritization of complete BGCs for therapeutic potential. This addresses genomic fragmentation and data volume challenges that hinder translating metagenomic BGCs into drug leads.

papers.title: Brewing Anxiety: Caffeine-Induced Thigmotaxis in Zebrafish Larvae.
papers.abstract: Thigmotaxis, or edge preference, is widely used as a measure of anxiety in vertebrate model systems. However, variability in this behavior limits its utility as a scalable measure for anxiolytic drug discovery. In the current study, we examine caffeine-induced thigmotaxis, using 5-day-old zebrafish larvae as a model system.
papers.summary: This study examines caffeine-induced thigmotaxis (edge preference) as a measure of anxiety in 5-day-old zebrafish larvae, aiming to address variability issues that limit its use in anxiolytic drug discovery. The work evaluates whether this behavioral assay can serve as a scalable screening tool for anxiety-related compounds.

papers.title: Anti-Inflammatory Activity of Cotula cinerea Essential Oil: Integrated Chemical, In Vivo, Histological, and Computational Evaluation.
papers.abstract: The anti-inflammatory activity of Cotula cinerea essential oil (EO) was evaluated using integrated chemical, in vivo, histological, and computational approaches. Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) identified trans-thujone (51.86%), santolina triene (10.60%), and sabinene (6.17%) as the most abundant constituents. In benzylthiouracil (BTU)-treated Wistar rats, EO administration reduced the liver and kidney indices from 4.36% to 2.70% and from 0.65% to 0.52%, respectively; red blood cell count increased from 4.90 to 7.17 × 1012/L and hemoglobin from 9.40 to 15.40 g/dL. Aspartate aminot
papers.summary: This study evaluates the anti-inflammatory properties of Cotula cinerea essential oil using chemical profiling (GC-MS), in vivo rat experiments, histological analysis, and computational modeling. The oil, rich in trans-thujone, reduced liver and kidney inflammation indices and improved red blood cell and hemoglobin levels in treated rats. Computational docking supports the observed biological activity.

papers.title: Synthesis and Cytotoxic Activity of 1,3-Selenazole-2-Amine Derivatives With Computational ADMET Profiling.
papers.abstract: A set of newly developed 1,3-selenazole-2-amine derivatives (1-4) was prepared via a modified Hantzsch-type cyclization of appropriately substituted α-bromoacetophenones with selenourea under reflux conditions. The synthesized compounds were tested for cytotoxic activity in HT-29 (colon cancer), MCF-7 (breast cancer), and L929 (mouse fibroblast) cell lines using the MTT assay. The compounds induced weak to moderate cytotoxicity in MCF-7 cells. Among them, compound 4 showed cytotoxic activity with IC50 value of 171.10 µM, while no appreciable activity was observed against HT-29 cells (IC50 > 30
papers.summary: This paper reports the synthesis of four new 1,3-selenazole-2-amine derivatives via a modified Hantzsch-type cyclization and evaluates their cytotoxicity against colon cancer (HT-29), breast cancer (MCF-7), and normal fibroblast (L929) cell lines. The compounds showed only weak to moderate activity, with the best compound (4) having an IC50 of 171.10 µM against MCF-7 and no appreciable activity against HT-29. Computational ADMET profiling was also performed to assess drug-likeness.

papers.title: Exploring the Neuropharmacological Potential of Ligustrum sinense Relevant to Parkinson's Disease: In Vivo and In Silico Study.
papers.abstract: Medicinal plants are valuable sources of bioactive compounds with potential applications in neurodegenerative disorders. This study investigated the antioxidant, neuropharmacological, and monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitory activities of Ligustrum sinense (L. sinense) leaf extract through in vitro, in vivo, and in silico approaches. Antioxidant activity assessed by the DPPH assay demonstrated moderate free radical scavenging capacity (IC50 = 73.56 ± 2.18 µg/mL) compared with l-ascorbic acid (IC50 = 7.29 ± 2.86 µg/mL). Behavioral evaluations using the open field, hole cross, elevated plus maze,
papers.summary: This study evaluates leaf extracts of the medicinal plant Ligustrum sinense for antioxidant, neuropharmacological, and monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitory activities using in vitro, in vivo, and in silico methods, with relevance to Parkinson's disease. The extract showed moderate antioxidant activity and behavioral effects in rodent models, with computational docking suggesting interactions with MAO. The findings support further investigation of L. sinense as a source of neuroactive compounds, though the evidence remains preliminary.

papers.title: Combating antimicrobial resistance through multimodal data via artificial intelligence.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a critical global health challenge, leading to substantial mortality and economic losses without science-based interventions. Conventional approaches to combating AMR have important limitations in addressing this escalating threat. Recent advances in AI, including deep learning, large language models, and protein language models, provide new opportunities to integrate multimodal data for AMR research. However, evidence remains uneven, with many approaches limited to computational benchmarking rather than real-world validation. Here, we critically review AI
papers.summary: This review critically examines how artificial intelligence—including deep learning, large language models, and protein language models—can integrate multimodal data to combat antimicrobial resistance. It highlights that while these approaches offer new opportunities, much of the evidence remains limited to computational benchmarking rather than real-world validation.

papers.title: Corrigendum to "Computational screening of Sophora flavescens phytochemicals as potential aromatase inhibitors: Molecular docking, ADMET, Network pharmacology, Molecular dynamics simulation, and DFT studies" [Pharmaceutic. Sci. Adv. 4 (2026) 100108].
papers.abstract: [This corrects the article DOI: 10.1016/j.pscia.2026.100108.].
papers.summary: This is a corrigendum correcting the original article on computational screening of Sophora flavescens phytochemicals as aromatase inhibitors. It does not present new research findings, but rather provides corrections to the previously published work.

papers.title: Computational evaluation of EPA-PC binding to GCase in neuronopathic Gaucher disease.
papers.abstract: Gaucher disease (GD) is a lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficient acid β-glucosidase (GCase) activity and consequent accumulation of glucosylceramide. Current enzyme replacement and substrate reduction therapies improve several systemic manifestations but have limited impact on neuronopathic disease, motivating evaluation of alternative molecular strategies. This study computationally assessed the interaction of EPA-phosphatidylcholine (EPA-PC), a marine-derived omega-3 phospholipid, with human GCase (PDB ID: 2NSX). The protein structure was examined by Ramachandran analysis and hydroph
papers.summary: This computational study used molecular docking and structural analysis to assess how EPA-phosphatidylcholine (EPA-PC), a marine-derived omega-3 phospholipid, binds to human acid β-glucosidase (GCase), the enzyme deficient in Gaucher disease. The work aims to explore alternative molecular strategies for neuronopathic Gaucher disease, where current enzyme replacement and substrate reduction therapies have limited efficacy. The findings suggest a potential binding interaction that could inform future therapeutic development, though experimental validation is needed.

papers.title: Advances in deep learning for antimicrobial research.
papers.abstract: The rapid spread of antimicrobial resistance and the lag in the development of new antimicrobial drugs have become major challenges for global public health. Conventional methods for discovering antimicrobial drugs are characterized by long development cycles and high costs, which are further exacerbated by the rapid evolution of bacterial resistance. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop efficient computational methods to accelerate the identification of drug resistance mechanisms and the research and development process of new antimicrobial drugs. In recent years, the new generation
papers.summary: This review surveys recent deep learning approaches applied to antimicrobial research, including the identification of resistance mechanisms and the discovery of new antimicrobial compounds. It highlights how computational methods can help overcome the long timelines and high costs of conventional antimicrobial drug development.

papers.title: AI-guided ethnopharmacology for cardiovascular drug discovery: from biomedical data to experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Despite substantial advances in pharmacological therapy, cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of mortality worldwide. Botanical drugs represent a rich source of structurally diverse bioactive metabolites, yet their translation into modern cardiovascular therapeutics remains limited by chemical complexity, incomplete mechanistic understanding, and challenges in experimental validation. Meanwhile, the rapid expansion of biomedical data resources and advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have created new opportunities to systematically investigate botanical drugs beyond empirical a
papers.summary: This review discusses how artificial intelligence can be integrated with ethnopharmacology to accelerate the discovery of cardiovascular drugs from botanical sources. It outlines a workflow from mining biomedical data resources through AI-driven prediction to experimental validation, addressing challenges like chemical complexity and incomplete mechanistic understanding of plant-derived compounds.

papers.title: A survey on ethical digital twins in healthcare.
papers.abstract: Digital Twins for Health (DT4H), defined as dynamic, data-driven, in silico representations of individuals, organs, medical devices, clinical workflows, or healthcare systems, are emerging as a promising paradigm for transforming healthcare. DT4H systems have the potential to advance personalized medicine, treatment optimization, disease prediction, drug discovery, clinical trials, and health system planning. However, their real-world development and deployment also raise important ethical, legal, and social implications (ELSI). Because DT4H systems rely on sensitive longitudinal health data a
papers.summary: This survey examines the ethical, legal, and social implications (ELSI) of Digital Twins for Health (DT4H), which are dynamic, data-driven virtual representations of individuals, organs, or healthcare systems. It highlights how these systems could advance personalized medicine, disease prediction, and clinical trials, while also raising concerns around sensitive longitudinal health data and real-world deployment. The paper provides a structured overview of these ethical challenges to guide responsible development.

papers.title: Analysis of novel umami peptides in Dengchuan beef and their taste mechanism: Integrated peptidomics, machine learning and molecular simulation studies.
papers.abstract: This study revealed the umami peptides in Dengchuan beef (DB) and its umami mechanism through peptidomics combined with molecular simulation technology. A total of 4220 peptides were identified by LC-MS/MS, among which five novel umami peptides (ER-10, GK-10, DR-11, EA-11, and HY-12) were screened via virtual screening. Sensory evaluation and electronic tongue analysis confirmed the umami properties of these peptides, with ER-10 and DR-11 exhibiting significant umami-enhancing effects. Molecular simulations revealed that Lys155, Gln52, Ser109, Ser216, Arg255, Ser217 and Met151 were identified
papers.summary: This study identified 4220 peptides from Dengchuan beef using LC-MS/MS peptidomics and screened five novel umami peptides (ER-10, GK-10, DR-11, EA-11, HY-12) via virtual screening and machine learning. Sensory and electronic tongue analyses confirmed their umami taste, with ER-10 and DR-11 showing strong umami-enhancing effects. Molecular simulations revealed key binding residues (Lys155, Gln52, Ser109, Ser216, Arg255, Ser217, Met151) underlying the taste mechanism.

papers.title: Cutting-edge developments in computer-aided anti-HIV drug design.
papers.abstract: Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS), caused by the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), remains a major global public health issue. Current antiretroviral therapy (ART) does not fully eradicate HIV infection, and the virus can establish latent reservoirs in the body that are challenging to eliminate. Consequently, the development of new anti-HIV medications remains a critical necessity. Traditional drug development methods are time-consuming, financially demanding, and carry a high risk of failure. In contrast, computer-aided drug design (CADD) offers a promising alternative by leveraging
papers.summary: This review examines recent advances in computer-aided drug design (CADD) approaches for developing new anti-HIV therapies, addressing the limitations of current antiretroviral treatments that cannot fully eradicate latent viral reservoirs. It highlights how computational methods offer faster, cheaper, and lower-risk alternatives to traditional drug development pipelines.

papers.title: Extra-nasal odorant receptors: molecular mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
papers.abstract: Since the first demonstration of extra-nasal odorant receptor (OR) function of OR1D2 (hOR17-4) in human sperm, ORs have emerged as a widely distributed receptor family. ORs are now known to be belonged to a family of seven transmembrane domain G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) expressed across diverse extra-nasal tissues, including skin, gastrointestinal tract, kidneys, cardiovascular system, liver, immune cells, and tumors. In these tissues, ORs act as metabolite- and environment-sensitive sensors that translate chemical cues into tissue-specific signaling pathways that regulate proliferati
papers.summary: This review discusses the emerging understanding of odorant receptors (ORs) expressed outside the nose, in tissues such as skin, gut, kidney, heart, liver, immune cells, and tumors. It highlights how these receptors act as chemical sensors that translate environmental and metabolic cues into tissue-specific signaling, with potential therapeutic implications.

papers.title: An interpretable consensus pipeline for candidate dopamine D2 receptor ligands.
papers.abstract: Machine learning accelerates GPCR ligand discovery but often lacks interpretability and struggles to generalise to structurally novel chemical space. We present an integrated framework combining ensemble learning, SHAP interpretability, and complementary structure-based analyses to prioritise putative candidates for the dopamine D₂ receptor (DRD2). Models were trained on 1247 curated ChEMBL compounds using Bemis-Murcko scaffold-split validation. Feature ablation showed that Morgan fingerprints alone were sufficient for classification (AUC = 0.910), whereas combined physicochemical descriptors
papers.summary: The authors built an interpretable machine-learning pipeline that combines ensemble learning, SHAP explainability, and structure-based analyses to prioritize candidate ligands for the dopamine D2 receptor. Using 1,247 curated ChEMBL compounds with scaffold-split validation, they found that Morgan fingerprints alone achieved strong classification performance (AUC = 0.910), suggesting physicochemical descriptors add little. The framework aims to improve generalizability to novel chemical space while remaining interpretable.

papers.title: Investigating the anticancer potential of phytochemicals from the mangrove Rhizophora mucronata as inhibitors of lung cancer-associated proteins: Insights from multiscale computational and in silico analyses.
papers.abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with a five-year survival rate of approximately 20-25% despite advances in targeted therapy and immunotherapy. There is a continuous need for novel, low-toxicity compounds capable of modulating key oncogenic pathways in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Mangrove ecosystems are rich reservoirs of bioactive phytochemicals, yet the inhibitory potential of compounds from Rhizophora mucronata against validated lung cancer-associated proteins has not been systematically explored using multi-scale computational approaches.
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking and simulation methods to screen phytochemicals from the mangrove plant Rhizophora mucronata as potential inhibitors of proteins associated with lung cancer. The authors identify candidate compounds that may bind key oncogenic targets in non-small cell lung cancer, suggesting these natural products warrant further experimental testing. The work is entirely in silico, so findings remain hypothetical until validated in vitro or in vivo.

papers.title: Preclinical identification of an oxadiazole-pyrazole lead targeting prostate cancer through integrated mechanistic evaluation.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality among men, while resistance to androgen deprivation therapy emphasizes the need for new therapeutic strategies. Molecular hybridization of pharmacologically relevant heterocycles offers a rational approach for developing novel anticancer agents.
papers.summary: This preclinical study identifies a novel oxadiazole-pyrazole hybrid compound as a lead candidate for prostate cancer treatment, developed through molecular hybridization of pharmacologically active heterocycles. The compound was characterized using integrated mechanistic evaluations, offering a potential new therapeutic option for patients resistant to androgen deprivation therapy.

papers.title: Mechanism-aware and safety-validated AI for drug repurposing: a critical review and translational pharmacology framework.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted drug repurposing seeks to identify new therapeutic applications for existing drugs. Nevertheless, most of the existing studies are centered on prediction scores and candidate ranking, and there is still relatively little attention paid to the pharmacological mechanisms, safety and translational validation.
papers.summary: This critical review argues that AI-driven drug repurposing has focused too heavily on prediction scores and candidate ranking while neglecting pharmacological mechanism validation, safety assessment, and translational testing. The authors propose a translational pharmacology framework that integrates mechanism awareness and safety validation into AI repurposing pipelines.

papers.title: Identification of natural TLR4 modulators through network pharmacology and molecular modeling in SARS-CoV-2 Acinetobacter baumannii co-infection.
papers.abstract: Viral-bacterial co-infection with SARS-CoV-2 and Acinetobacter baumannii exacerbates hyperinflammation via Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)-mediated immune pathways. Using network pharmacology, an integrated protein-protein interaction network identified 30 key inter-species hubs comprising viral, bacterial, and human host proteins, with TLR4 achieving a high MCC score (722), highlighting its high topological centrality as a host immune target. Virtual screen of 2,820 natural compounds against the TLR4/MD-2 complex identified three top candidates, CID5898023, CID5403474, and CID74977829, with docki
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology to identify TLR4 as a central host immune hub in SARS-CoV-2 and Acinetobacter baumannii co-infection, then virtually screens 2,820 natural compounds against the TLR4/MD-2 complex. Three top candidate compounds (CID5898023, CID5403474, CID74977829) were identified with favorable docking scores, suggesting potential natural modulators of TLR4-driven hyperinflammation.

papers.title: Structure-based multi-pocket virtual screening identifies FDA-approved candidate compounds targeting MPXV thymidylate kinase.
papers.abstract: Mpox, caused by monkeypox virus (MPXV), has emerged as a growing global health concern, yet effective targeted antiviral therapies remain limited. Thymidylate kinase (TMK), an essential enzyme required for viral DNA replication, represents a potential therapeutic target.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based virtual screening of FDA-approved compounds against multiple pockets of the monkeypox virus thymidylate kinase (TMK), an enzyme essential for viral DNA replication. The authors identify candidate drugs that could be repurposed as antiviral therapies for mpox, addressing the current lack of targeted treatments.

papers.title: Large-scale virtual screening of 17,967 IMPPAT phytochemicals identifies multiple CDR1 binders and reveals Apigenin-7-O-glucuronide as a putative CDR1-GSC1 dual-target lead against Candida albicans with initial in-vitro evidence.
papers.abstract: The increasing incidence of antifungal resistance in Candida albicans, mainly mediated by multidrug efflux transporters and alterations of cell-wall biosynthesis, requires the discovery of new antifungal compounds targeting multiple pathways involved in resistance. In the present study, we employed an integrated computational-experimental workflow to identify potential antifungal phytochemicals from the Indian Medicinal Plants, Phytochemistry and Therapeutics (IMPPAT) database. In the virtual screening, a total of 17,967 phytochemicals were screened against the ATP-binding cassette efflux tran
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study virtually screened 17,967 phytochemicals from the IMPPAT database against the Candida albicans efflux pump CDR1, identifying several binders and highlighting Apigenin-7-O-glucuronide as a dual-target lead that also binds GSC1, a cell-wall synthesis enzyme. Initial in-vitro experiments supported its antifungal potential, suggesting a promising scaffold for overcoming antifungal resistance.

papers.title: Designing novel linagliptin analogs through combined generative artificial intelligence, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and binding energy estimation for targeting fibroblast activation protein.
papers.abstract: Fibroblast activation protein (FAP) is a highly specific biomarker overexpressed in cancer-associated fibroblasts, making it a promising diagnostic target. Developing novel high-affinity molecular probes for FAP-targeted diagnostics remains an active area of research. In this study, an integrated computational pipeline combining generative artificial intelligence, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, binding energy estimation, and pharmacokinetic predictions was used to design and evaluate novel linagliptin-based compounds as potential FAP-binding analogs. From a preliminary
papers.summary: This study uses a computational pipeline combining generative AI, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and binding energy calculations to design novel linagliptin-based compounds that could bind fibroblast activation protein (FAP), a biomarker overexpressed in cancer-associated fibroblasts. The work aims to identify high-affinity molecular probes for FAP-targeted cancer diagnostics, though the abstract is truncated before reporting specific candidate compounds or results.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-driven drug discovery: a deep learning paradigm shift in pharmaceutical research and development.
papers.abstract: Efficient drug discovery is essential to mitigate the high attrition rates and capital-intensive nature of traditional pharmaceutical research. Deep learning (DL) has catalyzed a paradigm shift, offering unprecedented computational capabilities to accelerate this process. This review systematically summarizes advancements in DL methodologies for drug discovery. First, the critical data foundations, Molecular Representation Learning, and core architectures underpinning artificial intelligence (AI)-driven therapeutics are elucidated, with a particular emphasis on the evolution of generative AI f
papers.summary: This review surveys how deep learning is reshaping drug discovery, covering molecular representation learning, core neural network architectures, and generative AI approaches for therapeutic design. It argues that these computational methods can help reduce the high attrition rates and costs of traditional pharmaceutical R&D.

papers.title: Therapeutic Antitoxoplasmosis Potential of Garcinia cambogia: Evidence From In Silico and In Vivo Studies.
papers.abstract: Toxoplasma gondii, an opportunistic protozoan, is widely prevalent and poses potential health risks. Its treatment remains challenging with several side effects, urging the exploration of new, safe, and efficient drugs. We aimed to explore the therapeutic efficacy of the medicinal plant Garcinia cambogia (GC) against both acute and chronic toxoplasmosis. Sixty Swiss albino mice were allocated into five groups: I (healthy), II (model), III (spiramycin [SPM] treated, IV (GC treated), and V (SPM + GC treated). Each group is further divided into two subgroups receiving treatment at 4 and 42 days p
papers.summary: This study investigated whether the medicinal plant Garcinia cambogia (GC) could treat Toxoplasma gondii infection in mice, comparing it against the standard drug spiramycin alone and in combination. Using both computational (in silico) predictions and in vivo mouse experiments, the authors assessed therapeutic effects against acute and chronic toxoplasmosis. The findings suggest GC may have antitoxoplasmosis potential, though the abstract is truncated before reporting specific efficacy results.

papers.title: Drug Repurposing for Metabolic-Associated Fatty Liver Disease: Current Evidence, Challenges, and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) is a prevalent chronic liver condition with limited approved pharmacotherapies. Drug repurposing offers a time-efficient alternative to de novo development, yet existing reviews often compile candidate compounds without critically appraising the methodological robustness, evidence quality, or translational barriers. In this review, we evaluated current repurposing strategies, including real-world data analyses, computational screening, and experimental validations. As a preliminary search for this review, we searched PubMed and clini
papers.summary: This review critically evaluates drug repurposing strategies for metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD), covering real-world data analyses, computational screening, and experimental validation approaches. It highlights the methodological limitations and translational barriers that hinder progress in this field, arguing that existing reviews often list candidates without assessing evidence quality. The authors call for more rigorous appraisal to advance repurposing efforts toward clinical use.
